propositions: When a patch-set upload times out or defers during review, the reconcile_once function advances the persisted cursor to the newest event in the window unconditionally, permanently excluding abandoned candidates from future reconcile passes.

The Gerrit webhooks plugin delivers at-most-once (not at-least-once as documented), and abandoned webhook events are lost if the reconciler fails to vote on them in the same pass, leaving changes unvoted indefinitely until a manual recheck-review or rebase re-emits an event.

The reconciler must persist a low-water mark (minimum of newest event and oldest abandoned candidate time) so retryably-failed candidates re-enter the ?t1= window on subsequent passes and are re-driven automatically.

Terminal outcomes (voted, skipped with post_vote_closed reason) must advance the cursor; retryable states (error, deferred, review_timeout, reconcile_check_error) must hold the cursor back, bounded by RECONCILE_MAX_HOLDBACK_SECONDS to prevent poisoned candidates from pinning the window indefinitely.

Queue depth (how many changes are queued behind the current review) and held-back candidates must be observable via /health and reconcile_done telemetry so agents can distinguish bot-down, in-flight, queued, and dropped states.

The reconciler's double in test_review_bot.py recorded the since parameter but ignored it, allowing false-green tests that never exercised the production cursor filter on multi-event windows with mid-window failures.
